newsitem.title: INDIA: Russia Sukhoi jet best buy for India - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Russia Sukhoi jet best buy for India - analysts.

text.p: India has signed a contract to buy up to 50 Russian Sukhoi SU-30 MK fighter jets in a deal worth $1.8 billion, which defence analysts said on Sunday was the best it could have made to enhance defence capabilites.
"They are the best buy that India could have gone in for," Savita Pande, an analyst with the Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses in the Indian capital, told Reuters.
Indian news agencies said the Indian Air Force (IAF) would use the aircraft to replace seven-and-a-half combat squadrons by the year 2001.
Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav said India would purchase 40 Sukhoi SU-30 MK jets outright, the United News of India (UNI) reported.
Each aircraft would cost $40 million, UNI said, with delivery spread over five years, beginning this year.
State-run Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) would produce 200 more in India under a licensing arrangement with manufacturer Rosvooruzhenie, it added.

"They have long been in demand and constitute the front line air defence that we have been talking about for so long," Pande said. "I disagree with people who think Russian equipment is not up to the mark."

India currently has 799 combat aircraft, including British- designed Jaguars, French Mirage 2000s and Russian MiGs, including the 21, 23, 27 and 29, according to the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency reported from Moscow on Saturday that the deal was signed between the Indian defence ministry and the Rosvooruzhenie state arms exporter in the Siberian city of Irkutsk, where the jets will be built.
India was the first country to buy SU-30s, it quoted Rosvooruzhenie official Valery Pogrebnikov as saying.
The Sukhoi SU-30 MK is a high-performance multi-role warplane capable of deep penetration and long endurance, UNI quoted defence officials as saying.
The two-seat aircraft can carry up to eight tonnes of armament and has a combat range of 3,000 km (1,880 miles), which can increase to 5,200 km (3,250 miles) with inflight refuelling.
"It will plug the deficiencies that are bound to exist in an air force the size of the IAF," C. Uday Bhaskar, another defence analyst, said.
India has long been one of Russia's main arms buyers and Russian officials have said they hope the value of arms deals with India this year would grow to $3.5 billion.
The Indian defence delegation that signed the deal was also looking to buy new frigates, an aircraft carrier, air defence ships and submarines from Russia, UNI said.
